definition_zh: 不必要的；多余的；无谓的
definition_en: not needed, or more than is needed
core_image: 桌上已经堆满杯子，有人又端来一只
scene: 搬家那天车里最后一个空位塞满了纸箱，朋友们却还想把旧花盆也搬上去。Bringing that old pot along is quite unnecessary.
sceneCN: 这里 unnecessary 是「不必要的」（第 1 个义项：用不着、多此一举）；句意为把那只旧花盆带上其实完全没有必要。桌上多出杯子的画面，正是这个词的核心。

derivatives.zh: 形容词加 -ly 构成副词，义为「不必要地；多余地」
去掉否定前缀后的肯定形式，义为「必要的；必需的」
同根名词，义为「必要；必需品」
同根动词，义为「使成为必要」

senses.title: Not needed for a purpose
senses.definition: not required, because the purpose can be achieved without it
senses.definitionCN: 不需要的，因为不用它也能达到目的
senses.example: Another copy of the report is unnecessary, since we already have two.
senses.exampleCN: 报告再印一份没必要，我们已经有两份了。
senses.why: The prefix says not, and the base word names what cannot be done without; so the whole word names what can be done without.
senses.whyCN: 前缀 un- 表示「不」，词根指「离不开的东西」；合在一起就是「不用它也行」的东西。

senses.title: More than the situation calls for
senses.definition: extra, beyond what a situation needs or deserves
senses.definitionCN: 多出来的，超出情境所需或应有的限度
senses.example: He was asked to cut the unnecessary detail from the report.
senses.exampleCN: 他被要求删掉报告里多余的细节。
senses.why: Once a thing is not needed, anything beyond it becomes surplus, and this surplus sense grows straight out of the core image.
senses.whyCN: 既然用不着，那么超出所需的部分自然就成了多余之物，这层「过量」义正是从核心意象长出来的。

senses.title: Risk that could have been avoided
senses.definition: used of a risk or danger that could easily be avoided
senses.definitionCN: 形容本来很容易避免的风险或危险
senses.example: Driving after midnight was an unnecessary risk.
senses.exampleCN: 半夜开车是无谓的冒险。
senses.why: A person adds what is not needed and thereby adds danger; the word then attaches to the danger itself.
senses.whyCN: 人加了用不着的东西，也就多添了危险；于是这个词也用在了危险本身上。

senses.title: Words or actions that make things worse
senses.definition: used of a remark or move that causes trouble without helping
senses.definitionCN: 形容带来麻烦却毫无帮助的话语或举动
senses.example: His remark about her accent was unnecessary and hurt her.
senses.exampleCN: 他拿她的口音说事，那句话既多余又伤人。
senses.why: Speech that adds nothing is the same surplus as an extra cup on a full table, and here the surplus costs someone pain.
senses.whyCN: 对事情毫无帮助的话，就跟满桌之上再添一只杯子一样多余，只是这一次多余还让别人受了伤。

senses.title: Unlike what one would expect in logic
senses.definition: used in logic and argument for a condition that is not required for the result
senses.definitionCN: 在逻辑与论证中指对结论并不构成必需的条件
senses.example: The third assumption is unnecessary for the proof to hold.
senses.exampleCN: 这个证明的成立并不需要第三条假设。
senses.why: Strip away everything a result does not require, and what remains is exactly what unnecessary means in logic.
senses.whyCN: 把一个结论所不需要的东西全部剥掉，剩下的正是逻辑上所说的「非必需」。

intro.en: A simple English compound: the negative prefix un- over an adjective borrowed from Latin through French.
intro.cn: 一个简单的英语复合词：否定前缀 un- 加在经由法语借入的拉丁系形容词之上。

items.en: The prefix un- is native and marks the opposite of a word.
items.cn: 前缀 un- 为英语本土成分，用来表示一个词的反面。

items.en: Necessarius meant unavoidable or pressing, from necesse, that which cannot be otherwise.
items.cn: necessarius 意为「不可避免的、紧迫的」，源自 necesse（别无他法之事）。

items.en: The adjective came into French as necessaire and was attached to ordinary needs.
items.cn: 这个词以 necessaire 的形式进入法语，用于日常所需之物。

items.en: Necessary enters English in the fourteenth century and takes the negative prefix shortly after.
items.cn: necessary 于十四世纪进入英语，随后很快加上否定前缀。

items.en: Unnecessary also settles into logic and style manuals, where it labels what a proof or a sentence does not require.
items.cn: unnecessary 后来又进入逻辑学与写作手册，用来标出证明或句子不需要的东西。

note.en: The look-alike group collects forms built on the same necesse stem, and the near-meaning group collects surplus words.
note.cn: 形近组收集同一个 necesse 词干上的各种形式，近义组汇集表示多余过剩的词。

entries.definition: in a way that is not needed
something that cannot be done without
no longer needed because there is already enough
more than is wanted or required

normalIntro.en: The word is transparent: a negative prefix laid over the everyday word for what cannot be done without.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词十分透明：一个否定前缀压在日常表示「离不开」的词上。

normal.en: Un- plus necessary: what is not necessary is unnecessary.
normal.cn: un- 加 necessary：不是必需的，就是 unnecessary。

normal.en: It is unnecessary to do something is the standard sentence frame.
normal.cn: it is unnecessary to do 是标准句型框架。

normal.en: The adverb unnecessarily often appears with verbs of complaining and spending.
normal.cn: 副词 unnecessarily 常与抱怨、花费类动词连用。

normal.en: Necessary, necessity, and necessitate all share the Latin stem necesse.
normal.cn: necessary、necessity、necessitate 共享拉丁词干 necesse。

normal.en: Formal writing prefers unnecessary to unneeded.
normal.cn: 正式写作里更常用 unnecessary 而不是 unneeded。

abstract.en: See a third cup placed on a table that already holds two.
abstract.cn: 想象一张已有两只杯子的桌上又放下第三只。

abstract.en: Hear a joke told twice, then a long silence.
abstract.cn: 听一个笑话被讲了两遍，然后是一阵长久的沉默。

abstract.en: Feel a suitcase that will not close because someone packed for a longer trip.
abstract.cn: 体会一只因有人按更长的旅程收拾而合不上的行李箱。

examples.en: The extra meeting was unnecessary, since everyone had already agreed.
examples.cn: 那次额外会议没必要，因为大家早已达成一致。

examples.en: Staying until midnight was an unnecessary risk, and she regretted it.
examples.cn: 待到半夜是无谓的冒险，她后来很后悔。

examples.en: The editor removed every unnecessary word from the paragraph.
examples.cn: 编辑删掉了这一段里每一个多余的词。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「俺必需品」——东西已经够了还往包里塞，多带的那些俺自己也知道用不着。

root: 英语本土构词：前缀 un-（不）+ necessary（必需的），necessary 源自拉丁语 necessarius / necesse（不是别的选择、无法避免），经古法语 necessaire 进入英语

sensesIntro.en: From one core point, what can be done without, the word spreads to surplus, needless risk, useless remarks, and logic.
sensesIntro.cn: 从一个核心点「不用它也行」出发，这个词扩展到多余、无谓风险、无用之言与逻辑。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: one more cup on an already full table.
core.cn: 核心意象：已经摆满的桌上又放下一只杯子。

branches.en: The plain branch: the job is done without it.
branches.cn: 朴素分支：不用它事情照样办成。

branches.en: The surplus branch: more than the situation allows for.
branches.cn: 过剩分支：超出情境所需的部分。

branches.en: The risk branch: danger added for no gain.
branches.cn: 风险分支：毫无收益地添上的危险。

branches.en: The remark branch: words that add nothing and hurt.
branches.cn: 言语分支：毫无帮助还伤人的话。

branches.en: The logic branch: a condition the proof never uses.
branches.cn: 逻辑分支：证明从未用到的条件。

intro.en: A Germanic negative prefix plus a borrowed adjective whose own parts are easy to read.
intro.cn: 一个日耳曼语否定前缀，加上一个部件清晰的借入形容词。

latinIntro.en: The Latin stem is necesse, that which cannot be otherwise, with the adjective ending -arius.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁词干为 necesse（别无他法之事），加上形容词词尾 -arius。

items.meaningCN: 在 necesse 中表示否定的成分
items.example: Necesse is built on an old negative element.
items.exampleCN: necesse 由古老的否定成分构成。

items.meaningCN: 表示性质或状态的名词后缀

latinEntries.meaningCN: 不可避免的；别无他法的
不可避免的；不可或缺的

definition_zh: 令人不快的；不舒服的；不客气的；使人为难的
definition_en: not enjoyable or comfortable, or rude and unfriendly
core_image: 刚端起汤碗就闻到一股馊味
scene: 公交车在雨天挤得满当当，有人把滴着水的伞搁在别人裤脚上。The damp smell made the ride distinctly unpleasant.
sceneCN: 这里 unpleasant 是「令人不快的」（第 1 个义项：让人不舒服、不愉快）；句意为潮湿的气味让这趟车程明显令人难受。端起汤碗闻到馊味的画面，正是这个词的核心。

derivatives.zh: 形容词加 -ly 构成副词，义为「令人不快地；不客气地」
形容词加 -ness 构成名词，义为「不愉快；不快之事」
去掉否定前缀后的肯定形式，义为「令人愉快的」
同源动词，义为「使高兴；取悦」

senses.title: Something that is not enjoyable to the senses
senses.definition: not enjoyable to see, hear, smell, or touch
senses.definitionCN: 在视觉、听觉、嗅觉或触觉上让人难受
senses.example: There was an unpleasant smell from the drain.
senses.exampleCN: 下水道里冒出一股难闻的气味。
senses.why: The prefix means not and the base means pleasing, so the word starts as simply the negative of pleasant.
senses.whyCN: 前缀 un- 表示「不」，词根本义是「令人愉快的」，因此这个词起初就是 pleasant 的反面。

senses.title: Something bad that arrives without warning
senses.definition: used of news, surprises, or events that one would rather not have
senses.definitionCN: 形容人们宁可不发生的消息、意外或事件
senses.example: The test results came as an unpleasant surprise.
senses.exampleCN: 检验结果成了一个不愉快的意外。
senses.why: Anything that spoils pleasure is unpleasant, and bad news spoils it in one stroke.
senses.whyCN: 凡是把愉悦一扫而空的东西就是令人不快的，坏消息正是一下子把它扫空。

senses.title: A person who is rude or hard to deal with
senses.definition: used of a person whose manner is rude or unkind
senses.definitionCN: 形容说话行事无礼、刻薄的人
senses.example: The clerk was unpleasant to the old man at the counter.
senses.exampleCN: 柜台后的店员对那位老人很不客气。
senses.why: A person's manner of displeasing others is named by the same adjective that names the experience.
senses.whyCN: 一个人让别人不痛快的那种态度，也用同一个形容词来命名。

senses.title: A task or duty that one dreads
senses.definition: used of work that is boring, dirty, or upsetting
senses.definitionCN: 形容无聊、肮脏或令人难受的工作
senses.example: Cleaning the drains is an unpleasant task nobody volunteers for.
senses.exampleCN: 清理下水道是件没人主动愿意干的烦人活。
senses.why: Duty has no smell, yet it can be felt as the same sourness in the nose from the core image.
senses.whyCN: 职责本身没有气味，但做起来时鼻子里的那股酸味是一样的。

senses.title: An awkward situation that embarrasses people
senses.definition: used of situations that make those involved feel awkward
senses.definitionCN: 形容让在场的人都感到尴尬的处境
senses.example: Asking about the money put her in an unpleasant position.
senses.exampleCN: 问起那笔钱让她陷入很为难的处境。
senses.why: When an external thing causes inner discomfort, the discomfort moves into the situation itself.
senses.whyCN: 当外物带出内心不适时，这种不适就转移到了处境本身。

intro.en: Another plain negative compound, this time over an adjective that descends from Latin placere, to please.
intro.cn: 又一个朴素的否定复合词，这次压在源自拉丁语 placere（使高兴）的形容词之上。

items.en: The native prefix un- is added to borrowings to reverse their meaning.
items.cn: 本土前缀 un- 被加到借词上以反转其词义。

items.en: Placere meant to please or to be acceptable, with the adjective placidus, calm and pleasing.
items.cn: placere 意为「取悦、被接受」，形容词 placidus 意为「平和的、可喜的」。

items.en: Plaire brought the verb into French, and the present participle plaisant meant pleasing.
items.cn: plaire 把这个动词带入法语，现在分词 plaisant 意为「令人愉快的」。

items.en: Pleasant enters English from the French participle and describes what gives pleasure.
items.cn: pleasant 由这个法语分词进入英语，用来形容给人愉快的事物。

items.en: Unpleasant is formed by the negative prefix and extends from smells to people and duties.
items.cn: unpleasant 由否定前缀构成，并从气味扩展到人物与职责。

items.en: Its noun unpleasantness later becomes a polite word for a quarrel or an awkward scene.
items.cn: 其名词形式 unpleasantness 后来成为争吵或尴尬场面的委婉说法。

note.en: The look-alike group follows the please family, and the near-meaning group collects words for what we dislike.
note.cn: 形近组沿着 please 词族展开，近义组汇集表示令人嫌恶的词。

entries.definition: in a way that is not enjoyable

normalIntro.en: Everything about the word is familiar: an everyday negative prefix over the ordinary word for pleasure.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词的一切都很熟悉：日常的否定前缀压在日常表示愉悦的词上。

normal.en: Un- plus pleasant: the negative is taken directly from the positive.
normal.cn: un- 加 pleasant：否定直接取自肯定形式。

normal.en: An unpleasant smell and an unpleasant surprise cover the two most common collocations.
normal.cn: an unpleasant smell 与 an unpleasant surprise 覆盖了最常见的两类搭配。

normal.en: The adverb unpleasantly is used mainly of weather, sounds, and smells.
normal.cn: 副词 unpleasantly 主要用于天气、声音和气味。

normal.en: The noun unpleasantness often means a quarrel rather than a feeling.
normal.cn: 名词 unpleasantness 常指一场争执，而不是一种感受。

normal.en: Pleasant, please, and pleasure share the Latin root placere.
normal.cn: pleasant、please、pleasure 共享拉丁词根 placere。

abstract.en: Smell soup that has stood too long in a warm kitchen.
abstract.cn: 闻一碗在热厨房里放久了的汤。

abstract.en: Sit beside a passenger whose wet umbrella drips on your shoe.
abstract.cn: 坐在一位湿伞往你鞋上滴水的乘客旁边。

abstract.en: Watch a room go quiet after someone asks the wrong question.
abstract.cn: 看一个房间在有人问错问题之后安静下来。

examples.en: An unpleasant smell came from the rubbish bin behind the kitchen.
examples.cn: 厨房后面的垃圾桶里冒出一股难闻的气味。

examples.en: He was asked to stay calm even when the customer was unpleasant to him.
examples.cn: 即使顾客对他很不客气，他也被要求保持冷静。

examples.en: Cleaning the cellar is an unpleasant task, but somebody must do it.
examples.cn: 清理地窖是件烦人的活，但总得有人干。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「俺不累死」——被派去干又脏又烦的活儿，嘴上说着俺不累死，心里早就不痛快了。

root: 英语本土构词：前缀 un-（不）+ pleasant（令人愉快的），pleasant 源自拉丁语 placere（使高兴）经古法语 plaisant 进入英语

sensesIntro.en: One sourness in the senses spreads to news, people, duties, and the awkward scenes those create.
sensesIntro.cn: 感官里的一股酸味，进而扩展到消息、人物、差事，以及这些带出的尴尬。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a smell at the nose that spoils the appetite.
core.cn: 核心意象：扑到鼻子里、把胃口赶跑的一股气味。

branches.en: The sensory branch: what offends smell, ear, or eye.
branches.cn: 感官分支：冲撞嗅觉、听觉或视觉之物。

branches.en: The news branch: the surprise nobody wanted.
branches.cn: 消息分支：谁都不想收到的意外。

branches.en: The person branch: manner that makes others wince.
branches.cn: 人物分支：让别人皱眉的态度。

branches.en: The duty branch: work that is dirty or dull.
branches.cn: 职责分支：又脏又闷的工作。

branches.en: The situation branch: a scene that leaves everyone stuck.
branches.cn: 处境分支：让所有人都僵住的一幕。

intro.en: A native negative prefix over a French adjective that goes back to a Latin verb of pleasing.
intro.cn: 本土否定前缀压在经由法语借入、可追溯至拉丁「取悦」动词的形容词上。

latinIntro.en: The Latin family is placere, to please, with placidus and the noun placitum behind it.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁词族以 placere（使高兴）为核心，其后有 placidus 与名词 placitum。

items.exampleCN: 这部电影让孩子们很高兴。

items.example: Pleasant comes from the French participle.

items.meaningCN: 表示状态或性质的名词后缀

items.exampleCN: 我们度过了一个愉快的夜晚。

items.example: The room smelled unpleasantly of smoke.
items.exampleCN: 房间里有一股难闻的烟味。

latinEntries.meaningCN: 约定之事；令人满意之事

definition_zh: 不合理的；不理智的；过分的；不公道的
definition_en: not fair or sensible, or going beyond what is acceptable
core_image: 有人非要在深夜里把音量调到最大
scene: 邻居把音箱搬到阳台上，说晚上开派对是理所当然的事。It seems unreasonable to play music so loudly at that hour.
sceneCN: 这里 unreasonable 是「不合理的」（第 1 个义项：讲不通、没道理）；句意为那个钟点把音乐放得那么响实在说不过去。深夜把音量调到最大的画面，正是这个词的核心。

derivatives.zh: 形容词加 -ly 构成副词，义为「不合理地；过度地」
形容词加 -ness 构成名词，义为「不合理；不通情理」
去掉否定前缀后的肯定形式，义为「合理的；讲道理的」
同源名词，义为「理由；理性」
同源名词，义为「推理；论证」

senses.title: Not guided by good sense
senses.definition: not based on good judgement, so that others cannot follow it
senses.definitionCN: 不建立在良好判断之上，别人无法理解
senses.example: It is unreasonable to expect an answer within an hour.
senses.exampleCN: 指望一小时内得到答复是不合情理的。
senses.why: The word is the negative of reasonable, whose base is reason, the power of working things out.
senses.whyCN: 这个词是 reasonable 的反面，而词根 reason 指的正是推想、讲道理的能力。

senses.title: Asking for more than is fair
senses.definition: used of demands or prices that go beyond what is fair
senses.definitionCN: 形容提出过分要求或开出过高价格
senses.example: The hotel charges an unreasonable price for breakfast.
senses.exampleCN: 这家旅馆的早餐要价过高。
senses.why: Once a demand stops following reason, it also stops respecting the fair line, and the excess sense follows.
senses.whyCN: 要求一旦不再讲道理，也就不再顾惜那条公平线，于是「过分」这层意思随之而来。

senses.title: A person who will not listen to sense
senses.definition: used of a person who refuses to be persuaded by argument
senses.definitionCN: 形容听不进道理、怎么劝都没用的人
senses.example: He became unreasonable when anyone mentioned the money.
senses.exampleCN: 谁一提到那笔钱，他就变得不讲道理。
senses.why: When a person cuts himself off from reason, the absence of reason becomes a trait of character.
senses.whyCN: 当一个人把自己和道理隔开，那份「没有道理」就变成了一种性格。

senses.title: Not fair to someone
senses.definition: used of treatment or rules that are unfair to a person
senses.definitionCN: 形容对某人不公平的对待或规矩
senses.example: The rules seem unreasonable to anyone working nights.
senses.exampleCN: 对任何上夜班的人来说，这些规矩都不公道。
senses.why: A rule that no sound reason supports is felt by the people under it as plain injustice.
senses.whyCN: 一条得不到正当理由支撑的规矩，落到受它管的人身上就是明显的不公。

senses.title: Not justified by logic
senses.definition: used of an argument or belief that does not follow from the evidence
senses.definitionCN: 形容论证或信念与证据对不上
senses.example: The conclusion is unreasonable because the evidence does not support it.
senses.exampleCN: 这个结论说不通，因为证据并不支持它。
senses.why: In argument the word narrows to its literal core: the steps of reasoning are missing.
senses.whyCN: 在论证中，这个词收窄到最字面的核心：推理的步骤缺失了。

intro.en: A negative prefix over an adjective built on reason, itself from Latin ratio through French.
intro.cn: 否定前缀压在由 reason 构成的形容词上，而 reason 经法语来自拉丁语 ratio。

items.en: The prefix un- is native and negates adjectives freely.
items.cn: 前缀 un- 为英语本土成分，可自由加在形容词前表示否定。

items.en: Ratio meant reckoning, account, and the faculty of reasoning.
items.cn: ratio 意为「计算、说明」，也指推理的能力。

items.en: Raison carried the same senses of account and judgement into French.
items.cn: raison 把「说明」与「判断」的意思带进法语。

items.en: Reason enters English meaning both a cause given and the mind that gives it.
items.cn: reason 进入英语时兼指「给出的理由」与「给出理由的心智」。

items.en: Reasonable and then unreasonable are formed, and the negative spreads to prices, demands, and people.
items.cn: 先有 reasonable，后有 unreasonable，否定义继而扩展到价格、要求与人。

note.en: The look-alike group follows the reason family, and the near-meaning group collects words of excess and unfairness.
note.cn: 形近组沿 reason 词族展开，近义组汇集表示过分与不公的词。

entries.definition: in an unfair or excessive way
a cause or the power to judge
the process of thinking things through
so silly that it cannot be believed

normalIntro.en: The word is the negative of an adjective everyone learns early, so its parts are plain.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词是人人早就会的形容词的否定形式，部件一目了然。

normal.en: Un- plus reasonable: not open to reason at all.
normal.cn: un- 加 reasonable：完全没法讲道理。

normal.en: An unreasonable demand and an unreasonable price are the two fixed collocations.
normal.cn: an unreasonable demand 与 an unreasonable price 是两个固定搭配。

normal.en: The adverb unreasonably often modifies refuse and complain.
normal.cn: 副词 unreasonably 常修饰 refuse 与 complain。

normal.en: Reason, reasonable, and reasoning share the Latin root ratio.
normal.cn: reason、reasonable、reasoning 共享拉丁词根 ratio。

normal.en: Legal English uses unreasonable of terms that no fair person would accept.
normal.cn: 法律英语里 unreasonable 指任何通情达理的人都不会接受的条件。

abstract.en: Hear loud music from a balcony long after midnight.
abstract.cn: 在过了午夜很久之后听见阳台上传来很响的音乐。

abstract.en: See a customer shout at a clerk over a coin.
abstract.cn: 看见有人为一枚硬币对店员大喊。

abstract.en: Feel your hand stop moving on a clock that will not agree.
abstract.cn: 感受你的手停在一只怎么也对不上的钟上。

examples.en: It is unreasonable to blame the driver for a delay he cannot control.
examples.cn: 把司机控制不了的延误怪在他头上是不合情理的。

examples.en: The shop was criticised for charging unreasonable prices during the festival.
examples.cn: 这家店因节日期间要价过高而受到批评。

examples.en: She refused to argue with a friend who had become unreasonable.
examples.cn: 她拒绝再跟一个已经听不进道理的朋友争论。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「俺不理事儿」——别人摆事实讲道理，俺不理那套，这种做法自然就显得不合理。

root: 英语本土构词：前缀 un-（不）+ reasonable（合理的），reasonable 由 reason 加 -able 构成，reason 源自拉丁语 ratio（计算、理性）经古法语 raison 进入英语

sensesIntro.en: One root idea, showing no trace of reason, branches into outrage, resistance, unfair treatment, and weak proof.
sensesIntro.cn: 一个根义「看不到道理」，分出过火、倔强、不公与推理站不住四路。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a hand turning the volume knob to its limit.
core.cn: 核心意象：一只手把音量旋钮拧到最顶。

branches.en: The logic branch: a request no sound mind could follow.
branches.cn: 事理分支：清醒的人都跟不上的要求。

branches.en: The excess branch: prices and demands past the fair line.
branches.cn: 过度分支：越过公平线的价格与要求。

branches.en: The person branch: a friend who stops listening.
branches.cn: 人物分支：一个不再听劝的朋友。

branches.en: The fairness branch: treatment that singles someone out.
branches.cn: 公平分支：只针对某人的对待。

branches.en: The argument branch: a conclusion that does not follow.
branches.cn: 论证分支：推不出来的结论。

intro.en: A native negative prefix and a word-forming suffix sit on the ordinary noun for reason.
intro.cn: 本土否定前缀与构词后缀都压在日常名词 reason 上。

latinIntro.en: The Latin source is ratio, reckoning, with the verb reri behind it, to think or suppose.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁来源是 ratio（计算），其后的动词 reri 意为「思考、推想」。

items.example: He gave no reason for leaving.
items.exampleCN: 他没有给出离开的理由。

items.meaningCN: 表示状态或性质的名词后缀

items.example: He objected unreasonably to every plan.
items.exampleCN: 他对每个计划都不讲道理地反对。
她给出了有理有据的回答。

definition_zh: 不稳的；摇晃的；颤抖的；不坚定的；不稳重的
definition_en: likely to move or fall, or changing and not dependable
core_image: 桌腿短了一截，桌面一直在轻轻晃
scene: 手术后第三天，老人扶着床沿想站起来，脚下却总是发飘。His walk is still unsteady after the operation.
sceneCN: 这里 unsteady 是「摇晃的」（第 1 个义项：站不稳、走不稳）；句意为手术后他走起路来仍然东摇西晃。桌面一直轻轻晃的画面，正是这个词的核心。

derivatives.zh: 形容词加 -ly 构成副词，义为「摇晃地；颤巍巍地」
形容词加 -ness 构成名词，义为「不稳；摇晃」
去掉否定前缀后的肯定形式，义为「稳的；平稳的」
肯定形式加 -ly，义为「平稳地；持续地」

senses.title: A support that moves under weight
senses.definition: not firm on its base, so that it moves when used
senses.definitionCN: 底座不牢，一用就晃动
senses.example: The ladder was unsteady on the wet floor.
senses.exampleCN: 梯子在湿滑的地上放不稳。
senses.why: The prefix means not, and steady comes from stead, a fixed place; unsteady is therefore without a firm place to stand.
senses.whyCN: 前缀 un- 表示「不」，steady 源自 stead（固定的位置）；因此 unsteady 就是「没有一个稳稳的立足点」。

senses.title: A body that cannot keep its balance
senses.definition: used of walking or standing that cannot keep balance
senses.definitionCN: 形容走路或站立时保持不住平衡
senses.example: He was still unsteady after the long illness.
senses.exampleCN: 久病之后他走路仍然摇晃。
senses.why: A body out of its stead is the oldest and most physical sense: no fixed place for the feet.
senses.whyCN: 身体离开了固定的位置，是这个词最古老也最具体的一层：脚下没有稳当地儿。

senses.title: A hand or voice that shakes
senses.definition: used of hands or voices that tremble from weakness or feeling
senses.definitionCN: 形容因虚弱或情绪而颤动的双手或声音
senses.example: Her unsteady hand spilled the water.
senses.exampleCN: 她发抖的手把水洒了出来。
senses.why: A hand without a firm place to rest shakes, just as the ladder without a firm base rocks.
senses.whyCN: 手找不到稳稳搁置的地方就会抖，这与梯子没有稳当底座就会摇是同一个道理。

senses.title: Behaviour that changes without warning
senses.definition: used of prices, growth, or behaviour that keeps changing
senses.definitionCN: 形容价格、增长或行为反复变化
senses.example: The unsteady demand made planning difficult.
senses.exampleCN: 起伏不定的需求让做计划变得困难。
senses.why: What rocks instead of holding a line gives the number-driven sense of a trend that will not stay level.
senses.whyCN: 摇来摇去而不沿一条直线的东西，就给出了「数值留不住水平」这层走势义。

senses.title: A decision or loyalty that wavers
senses.definition: used of faith or support that may give way at any moment
senses.definitionCN: 形容随时可能动摇的信念或支持
senses.example: Their unsteady support worried the campaign team.
senses.exampleCN: 他们摇摆不定的支持让竞选团队很担心。
senses.why: Support that is not fixed in place is the last extension: the same lack of a firm footing, now in feeling.
senses.whyCN: 没有固定下来的支持是最后一层延伸：还是那种缺了稳固落点的状态，只不过发生在心里。

intro.en: A native prefix over a very old adjective formed from the English noun stead.
intro.cn: 本土前缀压在由一个极古老的英语名词 stead 构成的形容词上。

items.en: Stede meant a place or position, and the adjective stedig meant placed, fixed.
items.cn: stede 意为「地方、位置」，形容词 stedig 意为「安置好的、固定的」。

items.en: The adjective now spelled steady already described what holds its place.
items.cn: 后来拼作 steady 的这个形容词，当时已经用来形容「守得住原位」的东西。

items.en: The spelling steady settles, and stead survives mostly in the phrase in someone's stead.
items.cn: steady 的拼写在这一时期定型，stead 则主要保留在 in someone's stead 这一短语里。

items.en: Unsteady is formed with the negative prefix and is used of ladders, feet, hands, and voices.
items.cn: unsteady 由否定前缀构成，用于梯子、脚步、手与声音。

items.en: The figurative senses grow in economics and politics, where unsteady means not dependable.
items.cn: 此后词义在经济学与政治中扩展出比喻用法，指「靠不住」。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers the stead family and its near neighbours in spelling, while the near-meaning group collects unstable words.
note.cn: 形近组汇集 stead 词族及拼写相近者，近义组汇集表示不稳定动摇的词。

entries.definition: in the place of another thing

entries.definitionCN: 不整洁的（只是拼写相近，词源不同）

normalIntro.en: The word rests on an old English noun for a place to stand, which still survives in everyday phrases.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词压在一个古老的英语名词「落脚处」上，这个名词今天仍活在日常短语里。

normal.en: Un- plus steady: steady goes back to stead, a place to stand.
normal.cn: un- 加 steady：steady 源自 stead，意为「落脚处」。

normal.en: Unsteady on one's feet is the most useful phrase for illness and age.
normal.cn: unsteady on one's feet 是谈论病弱与年老时最好用的说法。

normal.en: An unsteady hand and an unsteady voice keep the physical image for feeling.
normal.cn: an unsteady hand 与 an unsteady voice 把身体的画面留给情绪。

normal.en: The noun is unsteadiness, the adverb unsteadily.
normal.cn: 名词是 unsteadiness，副词是 unsteadily。

normal.en: Instead and steady both contain stead, though their senses differ.
normal.cn: instead 与 steady 都含 stead，但意思不同。

abstract.en: See a table shake because one leg lacks a small block.
abstract.cn: 想象一张桌子因一条腿缺了块小木片而晃。

abstract.en: Feel a hand on a rail after a long illness.
abstract.cn: 体会久病之后扶住栏杆的那只手。

abstract.en: Hear a voice rise and fall in the middle of a sentence.
abstract.cn: 听一句话说到中途声音忽高忽低。

examples.en: The old chair is unsteady, so do not lean on the back.
examples.cn: 这把旧椅子不稳，别往后靠。

examples.en: Her unsteady hand made the signature look strange.
examples.cn: 她发抖的手让签名看起来很奇怪。

examples.en: Growth in the sector has been unsteady since the spring.
examples.cn: 这个行业的增长自开春以来起伏不定。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「俺得死地」——脚下这块地若稳当，俺才敢站；找不着这样的地，身子就一直晃。

root: 英语本土构词：前缀 un-（不）+ steady（稳的），steady 源自晚期古英语 stedig，词根为 stede（地方、位置），与 stand 同出日耳曼语族

sensesIntro.en: One root idea, having no firm place, starts with furniture and feet and ends with markets and loyalty.
sensesIntro.cn: 一个根义「没有稳当的落脚处」，从家具与脚步一路走到市场与忠诚。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a surface that shifts under whatever rests on it.
core.cn: 核心意象：放在上面的东西一动就跟着晃。

branches.en: The physical branch: legs, ladders, and tables that move.
branches.cn: 实体分支：会动的桌腿、梯子与桌子。

branches.en: The balance branch: a body that cannot hold itself up.
branches.cn: 平衡分支：撑不住自己的身子。

branches.en: The trembling branch: hands and voices that shake.
branches.cn: 颤动分支：发抖的手与嗓音。

branches.en: The trend branch: numbers that will not stay level.
branches.cn: 走势分支：起起伏伏的数字。

branches.en: The loyalty branch: support that may tip at any time.
branches.cn: 忠诚分支：随时可能倒向一边的支持。

intro.en: A native negative prefix over an adjective built on a noun that English has had for over a thousand years.
intro.cn: 本土否定前缀压在由一个英语已用了上千年的名词所作的形容词上。

latinIntro.en: The word is not Latin; the nearest Latin relative of the idea is stabilis, standing firm.
latinIntro.cn: 这个词并非拉丁语；概念上最近似的拉丁词是 stabilis（站得稳的）。

items.example: He came in his brother's stead.

items.meaningCN: 表示状态或性质的名词后缀

items.example: He rose unsteadily to his feet.

definition_zh: 不成功的；失败的；落空的
definition_en: not achieving the result that was intended
core_image: 一扇门推了三次都没开
scene: 年轻人提前半年准备面试，结果名单公布时还是没能进去。He was unsuccessful in his attempt to join the team.
sceneCN: 这里 unsuccessful 是「不成功的」（第 1 个义项：没能达到目的）；句意为他那次想进这支队伍的尝试没有成功。推了三次都没开的门，正是这个词的核心。

derivatives.zh: 形容词加 -ly 构成副词，义为「不成功地；失败地」
去掉否定前缀后的肯定形式，义为「成功的」
同源名词，义为「成功」
同源动词，义为「成功；接替」

senses.title: Not reaching the goal
senses.definition: not achieving the aim one set out to reach
senses.definitionCN: 没有达到原先设定的目标
senses.example: The rescue attempt was unsuccessful, and the boat drifted on.
senses.exampleCN: 救援的尝试没有成功，船继续漂了下去。
senses.why: The word is the negative of successful, whose base success came to mean a good outcome.
senses.whyCN: 这个词是 successful 的反面，而 success 的本义已经变成「好的结果」。

senses.title: A request or application that is turned down
senses.definition: used of a formal request or application that is refused
senses.definitionCN: 形容正式申请或请求被拒绝
senses.example: His application for the scholarship was unsuccessful.
senses.exampleCN: 他的奖学金申请没有通过。
senses.why: An application is a formal attempt, and when it is refused the door simply does not open.
senses.whyCN: 申请是一种正式的尝试，被拒时那扇门就是没有开。

senses.title: Effort that brings no result
senses.definition: used of attempts that use effort but bring nothing
senses.definitionCN: 形容花了力气却毫无收获
senses.example: Their attempts to save the old tree were unsuccessful.
senses.exampleCN: 他们救那棵老树的努力白费了。
senses.why: The core image is effort pushing against a closed door, so the word naturally names work that yields nothing.
senses.whyCN: 核心画面是力气顶在一扇不开的门上，因此这个词自然用来形容花了力气却无所得。

senses.title: A person who has not yet succeeded in a field
senses.definition: used of a person who has not yet achieved recognition in a field
senses.definitionCN: 形容在某个领域尚未取得成就的人
senses.example: As an unsuccessful writer he taught school to pay the rent.
senses.exampleCN: 作为尚未成名的作家，他靠教书付房租。
senses.why: When the negative applies to a person, the idea shifts from the attempt to the standing that the attempt never brought.
senses.whyCN: 当否定落在人身上，这层意思就从「那次尝试」转到「尝试始终没带来的地位」。

senses.title: A search or test that finds nothing
senses.definition: used of a search, test, or trial that turns up no answer
senses.definitionCN: 形容查找、试验或审讯毫无答案
senses.example: An unsuccessful search for the key went on until dark.
senses.exampleCN: 找钥匙一直毫无结果，直到天黑。
senses.why: A search is an attempt aimed at a find, so a search that finds nothing is the same missed door.
senses.whyCN: 搜寻本就是奔着找到东西去的一次尝试，因此一无所获的搜寻还是那扇没开的门。

intro.en: A negative prefix over an adjective from Latin successus, a going up or a good outcome.
intro.cn: 否定前缀压在由拉丁语 successus（上升、好结果）来的形容词上。

items.en: The native prefix un- reverses the meaning of adjectives of any origin.
items.cn: 本土前缀 un- 可反转任何来源形容词的词义。

items.en: Succedere meant to come next or to go up from below.
items.cn: succedere 意为「随后而来」或「从下面升上去」。

items.en: The noun succès named the result of an affair, good or bad.
items.cn: 法语名词 succès 指一件事的结局，好坏皆可。

items.en: Success enters English in the sixteenth century and settles on the good outcome.
items.cn: success 于十六世纪进入英语，后来固定指「好的结果」。

items.en: Successful and then unsuccessful follow, first of events and later of people.
items.cn: 随后出现 successful 与 unsuccessful，先用于事件，后用于人。

note.en: The look-alike group follows the success family, and the near-meaning group collects words of failure and frustration.
note.cn: 形近组沿 success 词族展开，近义组汇集表示失败与落空的词。

entries.definition: a series of things one after another

normalIntro.en: The word is the negative of one of the most transparent adjectives in English.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词是英语里最透明的形容词之一的否定形式。

normal.en: Un- plus successful: the aim was set and not reached.
normal.cn: un- 加 successful：目标设在前面却没走到。

normal.en: Be unsuccessful in doing something is the fixed frame.
normal.cn: be unsuccessful in doing 是固定框架。

normal.en: An unsuccessful attempt and an unsuccessful application are the two common partners.
normal.cn: an unsuccessful attempt 与 an unsuccessful application 是两个常见搭配。

normal.en: Success, succeed, and succession all come from Latin succedere.
normal.cn: success、succeed、succession 都来自拉丁语 succedere。

normal.en: Weather reports say an overnight search proved unsuccessful.
normal.cn: 天气新闻里常说一夜的搜寻未能成功。

abstract.en: See a door that does not open after three pushes.
abstract.cn: 想象一扇推了三次都没开的门。

abstract.en: Watch a fishing boat come back with an empty net.
abstract.cn: 看一艘渔船带着空网回来。

abstract.en: Feel the small hesitation before you read a list of names.
abstract.cn: 体会在读名单之前的那一下迟疑。

examples.en: The first attempt to repair the bridge was unsuccessful.
examples.cn: 第一次修桥的尝试没有成功。

examples.en: She was unsuccessful in her application for a transfer.
examples.cn: 她的调动申请没有通过。

examples.en: Their search for the missing dog proved unsuccessful for two days.
examples.cn: 他们找那只走失的狗，两天都没有结果。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「俺塞成功」——怎么塞都塞不进去，成功俩字一直没能塞进手里。

root: 英语本土构词：前缀 un-（不）+ successful（成功的），successful 来自名词 success，success 源自拉丁语 successus / succedere（随之而来、由下升起）

sensesIntro.en: One idea, the aim was missed, covers attempts, applications, wasted effort, careers, and fruitless searches.
sensesIntro.cn: 一个意思「目标没落到手」，覆盖尝试、申请、白费力气、事业与毫无结果的查找。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a door that does not give way.
core.cn: 核心意象：一扇怎么推也不让开的门。

branches.en: The plain branch: the goal simply was not reached.
branches.cn: 朴素分支：目标就是没达到。

branches.en: The formal branch: an application comes back refused.
branches.cn: 正式分支：申请被退回来。

branches.en: The waste branch: effort that leaves nothing behind.
branches.cn: 落空分支：力气花完什么也没留下。

branches.en: The career branch: someone still waiting to be recognised.
branches.cn: 事业分支：仍在等被看见的人。

branches.en: The search branch: a hunt that turns up nothing.
branches.cn: 查访分支：一无所获的搜寻。

intro.en: A native negative prefix sits over a Latin-derived adjective whose own suffix is very common.
intro.cn: 本土否定前缀压在拉丁来源的形容词上，其自身的后缀非常常见。

latinIntro.en: The Latin source is succedere, made of sub- under and cedere to go.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁来源是 succedere，由 sub-（在下）与 cedere（走）组成。

items.example: Succedere begins with sub- before c moved.
items.exampleCN: succedere 在 c 前用了 sub- 的变体。
cedere 是 proceed 与 concede 的词根。

items.meaning: to come after or do well

latinEntries.meaning: to come after, to go up

definition_zh: 不整洁的；凌乱的；不修边幅的；条理不清的
definition_en: not neat, with things out of their proper places
core_image: 书桌上纸、笔、杯子挤成一堆
scene: 考完试的房间里，卷子摊在床上，袜子挂在椅背上。Her desk stays untidy even when she has no homework.
sceneCN: 这里 untidy 是「凌乱的」（第 1 个义项：东西没放回原处）；句意为她即便没有作业，书桌也总是乱糟糟的。桌上纸笔杯子堆成一团的画面，正是这个词的核心。

derivatives.zh: 形容词加 -ly 构成副词，义为「凌乱地；潦草地」
形容词加 -ness 构成名词，义为「凌乱；不整洁」
去掉否定前缀后的肯定形式，义为「整洁的」
肯定形式加 -ly，义为「整齐地」

senses.title: Things left out of their proper places
senses.definition: with objects scattered about instead of being put away
senses.definitionCN: 东西散放着而没有收归原处
senses.example: The kitchen was untidy after the family dinner.
senses.exampleCN: 一家人吃过饭后厨房乱成一团。
senses.why: The prefix means not and the base means neat and in good order, so untidy begins as the plain opposite of tidy.
senses.whyCN: 前缀 un- 表示「不」，词根本义是「整齐、有条理」，因此 untidy 起初就是 tidy 的简单反面。

senses.title: A person careless about appearance
senses.definition: used of someone whose clothes and hair are not looked after
senses.definitionCN: 形容衣着头发不加打理的人
senses.example: He came to the interview looking untidy.
senses.exampleCN: 他来面试时一副不修边幅的样子。
senses.why: What is true of a room is also true of clothing: things are not put where they belong.
senses.whyCN: 房间如此，衣着也如此：东西都没待在它该在的位置上。

senses.title: Writing that is hard to read
senses.definition: used of handwriting or work that is messy on the page
senses.definitionCN: 形容字迹或版面上乱糟糟的
senses.example: Her untidy notes were hard to copy.
senses.exampleCN: 她潦草的笔记很难抄。
senses.why: Ink spread over a page without a line is the same clutter, moved from a room to a sheet of paper.
senses.whyCN: 一笔笔墨落在纸上不成行，就是同一种杂乱，只不过从房间搬到了纸面。

senses.title: Thinking or a plan without order
senses.definition: used of ideas or plans that lack a clear structure
senses.definitionCN: 形容想法或计划缺少清晰结构
senses.example: The untidy argument lost the reader halfway.
senses.exampleCN: 这篇论证条理不清，读到一半就跟丢了。
senses.why: If objects can sit out of place, so can the steps of a thought, and this abstract sense follows directly.
senses.whyCN: 既然物件能不在原位，思绪的步骤也可以，这层抽象义就是这样顺势而来的。

senses.title: A situation that looks poorly managed
senses.titleCN: 不整齐的；显得没管好的
senses.definition: used of a business or process that looks badly organised
senses.definitionCN: 形容生意或流程显得管理不善
senses.example: The shop looked untidy and understaffed on a Saturday.
senses.exampleCN: 这家店星期六看上去乱糟糟的，人手也不够。
senses.why: A trade that is not kept in order looks untidy, just as a room does.
senses.whyCN: 一桩没人打理的生意看上去乱糟糟，这和一间房的道理一样。

intro.en: A native negative prefix on an adjective that goes back to an old word for time.
intro.cn: 本土否定前缀压在一个可追溯至古老「时间」词的形容词上。

items.en: The prefix un- is native and turns a word into its opposite.
items.cn: 前缀 un- 为英语本土成分，把一个词翻成反义。

items.en: Tid meant time or season, and the adjective tidlic meant timely or in good season.
items.cn: tid 意为「时间、时令」，形容词 tidlic 意为「及时的、合时令的」。

items.en: Tidy shifts from timely to neat, and its spelling settles in this period.
items.cn: tidy 从「及时」转为「整洁」，拼写也在这一时期定型。

items.en: Untidy appears with the sense of things out of order and leaves the old time sense behind.
items.cn: untidy 出现时已是「东西乱了次序」的意思，旧有的时间义被丢掉。

items.en: The word extends to dress, handwriting, and plans that show no order.
items.cn: 此后这个词扩展到衣着、字迹以及毫无条理的计划。

note.en: The look-alike group follows the tidy family and similar un- spellings, while the near-meaning group collects messy words.
note.cn: 形近组沿 tidy 词族及相似的 un- 拼写展开，近义组汇集表示杂乱的说法。

entries.definitionCN: 不稳的（只是拼写相近，词源不同）

normalIntro.en: The word is the familiar negative of an everyday adjective, and its history lies in an old word for time.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词是日常形容词的常见否定形式，其历史藏在一个古老的「时间」词里。

normal.en: Un- plus tidy: the positive word means neat and in order.
normal.cn: un- 加 tidy：肯定形式意为整齐有序。

normal.en: An untidy room and an untidy desk are the most frequent collocations.
normal.cn: an untidy room 与 an untidy desk 是最常见的搭配。

normal.en: Tidy itself once meant timely, which explains why neat things are in season.
normal.cn: tidy 本义为「合时令」，这解释了为什么整洁东西总在恰当的时候出现。

normal.en: The noun is untidiness, the adverb untidily.
normal.cn: 名词是 untidiness，副词是 untidily。

normal.en: Messy is more spoken, untidy more neutral in writing.
normal.cn: messy 更口语，untidy 在书面中更中性。

abstract.en: See a desk with papers sliding into a pile.
abstract.cn: 想象一张桌子，纸片一点点滑成一堆。

abstract.en: Notice a tie worn with a shirt that is not ironed.
abstract.cn: 注意一条领带配着没熨平的衬衫。

abstract.en: Hear a drawer being pushed shut on clothes that will not fit.
abstract.cn: 听抽屉被硬推着关上，衣服塞不进去。

examples.en: His room is always untidy, with books on the floor.
examples.cn: 他的房间总是很乱，书都摊在地上。

examples.en: She came to the meeting looking untidy and out of breath.
examples.cn: 她来开会时一副不修边幅、气喘吁吁的样子。

examples.en: The untidy handwriting made the list hard to read.
examples.cn: 潦草的字迹让这份名单很难辨认。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「俺太脏」——屋里东西堆得乱，自己也不好意思，只能承认俺这屋实在太乱。

root: 英语本土构词：前缀 un-（不）+ tidy（整洁的），tidy 源自中古英语 tidy，再往上为古英语 tid（时间、时令）加上形容词词尾 -y，本义「合时令的」

sensesIntro.en: One core state, objects outside their proper place, spreads from rooms to clothes, writing, plans, and business.
sensesIntro.cn: 一个核心状态「东西不在原位」，从房间蔓延到衣着、字迹、计划与生意。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a desk where papers, pens, and cups have piled up.
core.cn: 核心意象：纸、笔与杯子在桌上堆成一团。

branches.en: The room branch: things never got put back.
branches.cn: 房间分支：东西一直没收回去。

branches.en: The person branch: clothes and hair left as they are.
branches.cn: 人物分支：衣着头发都随它去。

branches.en: The page branch: letters that will not stand in line.
branches.cn: 页面分支：字母站不成行。

branches.en: The mind branch: steps of a plan in no fixed order.
branches.cn: 思路分支：计划步骤没有固定次序。

branches.en: The business branch: a process nobody has organised.
branches.cn: 经营分支：没人管过流程的事。

intro.en: A native negative prefix over an adjective whose root once named a point in time.
intro.cn: 本土否定前缀压在一个词根曾指「时节」的形容词上。

latinIntro.en: The root is Germanic rather than Latin; the closest Latin idea is tempus, time.
latinIntro.cn: 这个词根属日耳曼语而非拉丁语；概念上最近的拉丁词是 tempus（时间）。

items.example: Tid survives in the word tidings.
items.exampleCN: tid 仍存在于 tidings 一词中。

items.meaningCN: 表示状态或性质的名词后缀

items.example: Papers lay untidily on the floor.

definition_zh: 直到；到……为止；直到……才；（否定句）直到……才
definition_en: up to the time when something happens or ends
core_image: 走廊尽头的灯一直亮着，亮到门开为止
scene: 母亲坐在客厅没关灯，说要等孩子进门她才去睡。She waited in the hall until the last bus arrived.
sceneCN: 这里 until 是「直到……为止」（第 1 个义项：动作持续到某时）；句意为她在门厅一直等到末班车到达。走廊的灯亮到门开为止的画面，正是这个词的核心。

derivatives.zh: 同义的较短形式，义为「直到」，口语中更常用
形近但不同源，义为「不合时宜的」（只是拼写相近，词源不同）

senses.title: Action that continues up to a point in time
senses.definition: used to say that an action goes on and stops at a certain time
senses.definitionCN: 表示动作持续进行，到某一时间停止
senses.example: The shop stays open until nine.
senses.exampleCN: 这家店开到九点。
senses.why: The word marks the end point of a stretch of time, and the thing before that point simply keeps going.
senses.whyCN: 这个词标出一段时间的终点，在此之前的事情就一直在持续。

senses.title: Not before a certain time
senses.definition: used with a negative or in a question to mean not happening before a time
senses.definitionCN: 与否定或疑问连用，表示在某一时间之前没有发生
senses.example: He did not answer until the third knock.
senses.exampleCN: 直到敲第三下他才应门。
senses.why: If a line marks where something stops, then nothing has happened on the near side of it; this is the negative reading.
senses.whyCN: 既然一条线标出某事停止的地方，那么线这一侧就还什么都没发生，这正是否定用法。

senses.title: A limit set on a rule
senses.definition: used of rules and notices that last up to a stated point
senses.definitionCN: 用于规定或通告，表示有效到某一时点
senses.example: The office is closed until Monday.
senses.exampleCN: 办公室关到星期一。
senses.why: A notice needs an end point, and the word supplies exactly the point where the rule stops.
senses.whyCN: 通告需要一个终点，这个词提供的正是规定停止的那一点。

senses.title: A change that finally comes
senses.definition: used when a state lasts and then finally gives way
senses.definitionCN: 表示某种状态一直持续，最后才改变
senses.example: The noise went on until someone complained.
senses.exampleCN: 吵闹一直继续，直到有人投诉才停。
senses.why: When a stretch is long, the moment it ends is also the moment something turns, so the word gathers a sense of turning.
senses.whyCN: 当这一段很长时，它结束的那一刻也正是事情转折的一刻，于是这个词带上了转折意味。

senses.title: Until then in narrative
senses.definition: used in stories for the time before an event happens
senses.definitionCN: 在叙述中指某事发生之前的那段时间
senses.example: Until that night, nobody in the village locked a door.
senses.exampleCN: 在那晚之前，村里没人锁门。
senses.why: In a story the same end point can be read backwards, naming all the time before the event arrives.
senses.whyCN: 在故事里，同一个终点也可以反着读，指事件到来之前的整段时间。

intro.en: An old compound preposition whose first part survives in our northern word for the same thing.
intro.cn: 一个古老的复合介词，其前一部分仍保存在同义的北方说法里。

items.en: The form und means up to, and the older Scandinavian words spread it into English.
items.cn: und 意为「直到」，更早的斯堪的纳维亚语形式把它带进英语。

items.en: Till was already used for up to a time, and it is not a shortened form of until.
items.cn: till 早已表示「直到」，它并不是 until 的缩写。

items.en: Untill appears as a reinforced till, with un- here meaning up to rather than not.
items.cn: untill 作为加强形式的 till 出现，此处 un- 意为「直到」，并非否定。

items.en: Until and till are used side by side, until being more formal in writing.
items.cn: until 与 till 并行使用，写作中 until 更正式。

items.en: Not until opens a clause and forces the main verb to come late, a favourite of formal prose.
items.cn: not until 引导从句并使主动词后置，是正式文章偏爱的结构。

note.en: The look-alike group collects time prepositions and similar spellings, while the near-meaning group compares end points.
note.cn: 形近组收集时间介词与相近拼写，近义组比较表示终点的时间词。

entries.definitionCN: 不合时宜的（只是拼写相近，词源不同）
身体不适的（只是拼写相近，词源不同）
除非（只是拼写相近，词源不同）

entries.definition: from a time in the past until now

normalIntro.en: A short, very old time word whose shape looks like a negative but is not one.
normalIntro.cn: 一个简短而古老的表示时间的词，它的样子像否定，其实不是。

normal.en: Until and till are equally old; neither is a clipping of the other.
normal.cn: until 与 till 一样古老，谁也不是谁截出来的。

normal.en: Not until with an inverted main clause is the formal pattern.
normal.cn: not until 加倒装主句是正式模式。

normal.en: From morning until night shows the stretch of time clearly.
normal.cn: from morning until night 清楚显示了时间的段距。

normal.en: Until further notice is the fixed phrase in notices.
normal.cn: until further notice 是通告里的固定说法。

normal.en: The un- here means up to, unlike un- in unhappy.
normal.cn: 此处的 un- 意为「直到」，不同于 unhappy 中的 un-。

abstract.en: Watch a hallway light burn until a door opens.
abstract.cn: 想象走廊的灯一直亮着，直到门打开。

abstract.en: Count three knocks before the chain is lifted.
abstract.cn: 数到第三下敲门声，链子才被摘下。

abstract.en: See a line drawn on a road, and a car stopping at it.
abstract.cn: 看路面上画着一条线，一辆车停在线上。

examples.en: We waited at the gate until the lights went out.
examples.cn: 我们在门口一直等到灯灭。

examples.en: She did not speak until the whole room was quiet.
examples.cn: 直到整个房间安静下来，她才开口。

examples.en: The road will stay closed until the bridge is repaired.
examples.cn: 这条路将封闭到桥梁修好为止。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「俺踢了」——等得实在不耐烦，俺踢了踢门框，一直踢到门开为止。

root: 中古英语 untill，由上古北欧语 und（直到）与 till（到……为止）结合而成；till 本身并非 until 的缩略，二者同义并行

sensesIntro.en: One function, marking the end of a stretch of time, yields the durative sense and the negative sense.
sensesIntro.cn: 一个功能「标出一段时间的终点」，生出持续义与否定义两路。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a bright line drawn on a road.
core.cn: 核心意象：路面上一条亮着的线。

branches.en: The duration branch: something goes on all the way there.
branches.cn: 持续分支：某事一路持续到那一点。

branches.en: The negative branch: nothing happens on the near side.
branches.cn: 否定分支：线这一侧什么都没发生。

branches.en: The notice branch: rules that last to a stated point.
branches.cn: 通告分支：规定有效到某个时点。

branches.en: The turning branch: a long state at last gives way.
branches.cn: 转折分支：长久的状态终于让位。

branches.en: The narrative branch: the stretch before an event.
branches.cn: 叙述分支：事件之前的那段时光。

intro.en: A small function word made of two old time markers fused together.
intro.cn: 一个由两个古老时间标记融合而成的小功能词。

latinIntro.en: The word is Germanic; the Latin adverb for up to this point is tenus, used with a genitive.
latinIntro.cn: 这个词属日耳曼语；拉丁语中表示「到此为止」的副词是 tenus，与属格连用。

items.example: Until keeps the older sense of un as up to.
items.exampleCN: until 保留了 un 意为「直到」的古义。

items.example: Not until noon did it stop raining.
The office is closed until further notice.
items.exampleCN: 办公室关闭，直到另行通知。

items.example: Up until last week he was here.
items.exampleCN: 一直到上周他都在这里。

definition_zh: 不寻常的；罕见的；与众不同的；特别的
definition_en: not common or ordinary, and therefore noticed
core_image: 一群灰鸽子中间落着一只白鸽
scene: 小镇的集市上忽然来了个戴高帽的卖艺人，围观的人越聚越多。It is unusual to see a crowd like this on a weekday.
sceneCN: 这里 unusual 是「不寻常的」（第 1 个义项：很少见、不是常态）；句意为工作日见到这么多人实在少见。灰鸽群中落着一只白鸽，正是这个词的核心。

collocations.phrase: for some reason unusual to us
collocations.zh: 对我们来说不同寻常的原因

derivatives.zh: 形容词加 -ly 构成副词，义为「异常地；格外地」
形容词加 -ness 构成名词，义为「不寻常；罕见」
去掉否定前缀后的肯定形式，义为「通常的」
肯定形式加 -ly，义为「通常」
同源名词，义为「习惯；使用」，派生路径见词源

senses.title: Not happening in the ordinary course
senses.definition: not happening as it normally does
senses.definitionCN: 没有按平常的情形发生
senses.example: It is unusual to find the library this empty.
senses.exampleCN: 图书馆空成这样实属少见。
senses.why: The prefix says not and the base says customary, because usual comes from use, a habit.
senses.whyCN: 前缀表示「不」，词根意为「惯常的」，因为 usual 源自 use（习惯）。

senses.title: Rare enough to be noticed
senses.definition: rare enough that people stop and look
senses.definitionCN: 罕见得让人停下来多看几眼
senses.example: An unusual bird landed on the roof.
senses.exampleCN: 一只少见的鸟落在屋顶上。
senses.why: What rarely happens stands out from the background, and the word easily takes on the sense of rare.
senses.whyCN: 很少发生的事会从背景里凸显出来，于是这个词自然带出「稀奇」的意思。

senses.title: Different from others in a good way
senses.definition: used with approval of something special or original
senses.definitionCN: 用于赞许某个特别或有创意的做法
senses.example: They chose an unusual route through the old town.
senses.exampleCN: 他们挑了一条穿过老城的别致路线。
senses.why: What separates itself from habit can separate itself well, so the word takes on approval of the original.
senses.whyCN: 与习惯拉开距离的东西也可能拉得漂亮，于是这个词带上了对「有创意」的赞许。

senses.title: Odd in a way that worries people
senses.definition: used of conditions or behaviour that suggest something is wrong
senses.definitionCN: 形容暗示出问题的状况或行为
senses.example: The doctor noticed an unusual rhythm in the pulse.
senses.exampleCN: 医生注意到脉搏有一种异常节律。
senses.why: Once something departs from the usual, a departure can also warn that something has gone wrong.
senses.whyCN: 一旦某物偏离常规，这种偏离也能成为「哪里出了毛病」的警报。

senses.title: Exceptional in degree
senses.definition: used with a following adjective to mean exceptionally
senses.definitionCN: 后接形容词，表示程度格外地
senses.example: The room fell unusually quiet when she entered.
senses.exampleCN: 她进门时，房间异常安静下来。
senses.why: A departure from the customary, applied to a degree, becomes the adverb sense of going beyond the normal level.
senses.whyCN: 偏离常规一旦用在程度上，就成了「超出平常水准」的副词义。

intro.en: A negative prefix on an adjective formed from the noun use in its old sense of habit.
intro.cn: 否定前缀压在一个由 use 旧义「习惯」构成的形容词上。

items.en: The prefix un- is native and marks the opposite of a quality.
items.cn: 前缀 un- 为英语本土成分，表示某一性质的反面。

items.en: Usus meant use or practice, with the verb uti, to use.
items.cn: usus 意为「使用、实践」，动词为 uti（使用）。

items.en: The noun passed into French as us, and the adjective usuel meant customary.
items.cn: 这个名词在法语中作 us，形容词 usuel 意为「惯常的」。

items.en: Usual settles in English meaning customary, derived from use as a habit.
items.cn: usual 在英语中定型为「惯常的」，其根源是「习惯」义的使用。

items.en: Unusual grows from that and widens to rare sights, odd behaviour, and unusual weather.
items.cn: unusual 由此生长出来，并扩展到罕见景象、反常行为与反常天气。

note.en: The look-alike group follows the use family and its adverbs, while the near-meaning group collects words for the rare and the odd.
note.cn: 形近组沿 use 词族及其副词展开，近义组汇集表示罕见与奇特的说法。

entries.definition: a habit or the act of employing

normalIntro.en: The word rests on use in the sense of a habit, which is why usual means customary.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词压在 use（习惯）的词义上，所以 usual 才表示惯常。

normal.en: Un- plus usual: not the way it usually goes.
normal.cn: un- 加 usual：不是通常的路数。

normal.en: It is unusual to find is a handy formal opener.
normal.cn: it is unusual to find 是很好用的正式开头。

normal.en: The adverb unusually also means exceptionally before adjectives.
normal.cn: 副词 unusually 放在形容词前还表示「格外」。

normal.en: Use, usual, and usually share the Latin root uti.
normal.cn: use、usual、usually 共享拉丁词根 uti。

normal.en: Unusual is neutral; strange often carries suspicion.
normal.cn: unusual 中性，strange 常带疑虑。

abstract.en: Pick out one white bird in a crowd of grey pigeons.
abstract.cn: 在一群灰鸽里挑出一只白鸽。

abstract.en: Hear a weekday market suddenly loud with drums.
abstract.cn: 听工作日的集市忽然响起鼓声。

abstract.en: Feel a hand made of ice when the others are warm.
abstract.cn: 体会一只在众多温暖手中格外冰凉的手。

examples.en: It is unusual for the train to arrive early.
examples.cn: 这趟车很少提前到达。

examples.en: The garden was full of unusual plants from the south.
examples.cn: 园子里满是南方来的稀奇植物。

examples.en: He gave the question an unusually long look before answering.
examples.cn: 他在回答前异常长久地看了看这个问题。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「俺幽若」——人堆里那个格外安静的人，俺一抬眼就看见了，因为太少见。

root: 英语本土构词：前缀 un-（不）+ usual（通常的），usual 源自拉丁语 usus / uti（使用、实践）及晚期拉丁 usualis，经古法语进入英语，本义「惯用的」

sensesIntro.en: One contrast with habit splits into the rare, the different, the worrying, and the exceptional degree.
sensesIntro.cn: 一个与「习惯」的对比，分出罕见、独特、反常与程度格外四路。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: one white bird standing among grey ones.
core.cn: 核心意象：灰鸽群里站着一只白鸽。

branches.en: The habit branch: this is not how it normally goes.
branches.cn: 习惯分支：平时不是这个样子。

branches.en: The rarity branch: people stop and stare.
branches.cn: 罕见分支：人们停下来张望。

branches.en: The praise branch: different in a welcome way.
branches.cn: 赞许分支：不同得让人欣然接受。

branches.en: The warning branch: a sign that something is off.
branches.cn: 警示分支：某个地方不对的信号。

branches.en: The degree branch: exceptionally, before an adjective.
branches.cn: 程度分支：放在形容词前表示格外。

intro.en: A native negative prefix over an adjective whose base noun still lives in common use.
intro.cn: 本土否定前缀压在一个底名词仍在常用词汇中的形容词上。

latinIntro.en: The Latin base is uti and its noun usus, from which usualis was formed.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁词根为 uti 及其名词 usus，usualis 由后者构成。

items.example: Custom is a kind of use.
items.exampleCN: 习俗即是一种习惯性的使用。

items.example: Usus gives usuel and then usual.
items.exampleCN: usus 派生出 usuel，再成为 usual。

items.meaningCN: 表示状态或性质的名词后缀

items.example: He came at the usual time.

items.meaning: the way words or things are used
items.exampleCN: 英语的用法在这里不同。

latinEntries.meaning: to use, to make use of

definition_zh: 不愿意的；勉强的；不情愿的；不肯的
definition_en: not wanting to do something, and doing it only with reluctance
core_image: 脚往前挪，身子却往后拽
scene: 孩子被叫去道歉，手扶着门框迟迟不肯松开。He was unwilling to admit that the mistake was his.
sceneCN: 这里 unwilling 是「不愿意的」（第 1 个义项：心里不想做）；句意为他怎么也不肯承认这错在自己。脚往前、身子后拽的画面，正是这个词的核心。

derivatives.zh: 形容词加 -ly 构成副词，义为「不情愿地」
形容词加 -ness 构成名词，义为「不愿；勉强」
去掉否定前缀后的肯定形式，义为「乐意的」
同源名词，义为「意志；意愿」
同源名词，义为「意志力」

senses.title: Not wanting to do something
senses.definition: not wanting to do a thing that one has been asked to do
senses.definitionCN: 对别人要求做的事心里并不想做
senses.example: He was unwilling to lend the car to anyone.
senses.exampleCN: 他不愿意把车借给任何人。
senses.why: The prefix says not and the base says having the will for something, so the word names a will that is absent.
senses.whyCN: 前缀表示「不」，词根表示「对某事有意愿」，因此这个词说的是「意愿缺位」。

senses.title: Doing it, but with resistance
senses.definition: doing something anyway, though clearly against one's wish
senses.definitionCN: 虽然做了，但明显违背自己的意愿
senses.example: The witness gave an unwilling answer.
senses.exampleCN: 证人勉强给出了回答。
senses.why: When the will is absent but the act happens anyway, the act carries the resistance inside it.
senses.whyCN: 意愿缺位而事情照样做了，这份抵触就留在了动作里。

senses.title: A role taken on without choice
senses.definition: used of people who are in a situation and never chose it
senses.definitionCN: 形容身处其中而从未自己选择的人
senses.example: He became an unwilling leader when the captain fell ill.
senses.exampleCN: 队长病倒后，他成了不情愿的领头人。
senses.why: A person who never wanted the part is still inside it, so the word comes to name the role itself.
senses.whyCN: 从没想要这个位置的人却仍身在其中，于是这个词也用来指这个角色。

senses.title: A refusal to accept a fact
senses.definition: used of refusal to admit or accept something true
senses.definitionCN: 形容不愿意承认或接受某个事实
senses.example: She was unwilling to believe the letter was real.
senses.exampleCN: 她不肯相信那封信是真的。
senses.why: Not wanting to act turns into not wanting to see, and the object of the will becomes a fact.
senses.whyCN: 不想做会转为不想看见，意愿的对象于是变成了一个事实。

senses.title: Slow response because of doubt
senses.definition: used of a slow or hesitant response that shows no enthusiasm
senses.definitionCN: 形容因犹疑而显得没有热情的反应
senses.example: There was an unwilling silence before he answered.
senses.exampleCN: 他回答之前有一段不太情愿的沉默。
senses.why: A will that pulls back shows in timing, so the word also describes answers that come late.
senses.whyCN: 退缩的意愿会从快慢上看出来，因此这个词也形容迟迟才到的回应。

intro.en: A native negative prefix on an adjective made from the old noun for will.
intro.cn: 本土否定前缀压在一个由古老的「意愿」名词构成的形容词上。

items.en: The prefix un- is native and negates a quality directly.
items.cn: 前缀 un- 为英语本土成分，直接否定某一性质。

items.en: The noun willa meant wish or desire, and willan meant to want.
items.cn: 名词 willa 意为「愿望」，动词 willan 意为「想要」。

items.en: The adjectives willing and unwilling are formed with the suffix -ing on will.
items.cn: 形容词 willing 与 unwilling 由 will 加词尾 -ing 构成。

items.en: Unwilling is fixed in the frame be unwilling to do, common in reports and statements.
items.cn: unwilling 固定在 be unwilling to do 这一框架中，常见于报告与陈述。

items.en: The noun unwillingness and the adverb unwillingly follow as regular forms.
items.cn: 随后按规律产生了名词 unwillingness 与副词 unwillingly。

note.en: The look-alike group follows the will family, while the near-meaning group collects words of reluctance and refusal.
note.cn: 形近组沿 will 词族展开，近义组汇集表示不情愿与拒绝的说法。

entries.definition: the power to decide or want

entries.definitionCN: 野生的（只是拼写相近，词源不同）

normalIntro.en: The word is built on the ordinary noun for the will, with a negative prefix and a participle ending.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词建在日常表示「意愿」的名词上，前面加否定前缀，后面加分词词尾。

normal.en: Un- plus willing: willing goes back to will, the wish to act.
normal.cn: un- 加 willing：willing 源自 will，即行动的愿望。

normal.en: Be unwilling to do is the frame to learn first.
normal.cn: be unwilling to do 是最先要记住的框架。

normal.en: An unwilling helper is someone who helps and resents it.
normal.cn: an unwilling helper 指帮了忙却满腹怨气的人。

normal.en: Unwilling is about will; reluctant is about hesitation of feeling.
normal.cn: unwilling 重在意愿，reluctant 重在情绪上的迟疑。

normal.en: The noun is unwillingness, the adverb unwillingly.
normal.cn: 名词是 unwillingness，副词是 unwillingly。

abstract.en: Watch feet step forward while the body leans back.
abstract.cn: 想象脚往前迈，身子却向后仰。

abstract.en: See a hand hold the door frame and not let go.
abstract.cn: 看见一只手扶着门框不肯松。

abstract.en: Hear an answer given a beat too late.
abstract.cn: 听一句慢了一拍的回答。

examples.en: The company was unwilling to change its rules.
examples.cn: 公司不愿更改自己的规定。

examples.en: An unwilling smile crossed his face when the bill arrived.
examples.cn: 账单送来时，他脸上掠过一丝勉强的笑。

examples.en: She unwillingly handed over the letter and left the room.
examples.cn: 她不情愿地交出那封信，离开了房间。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「俺不灵」——嘴上被派了活儿，心里觉得俺不灵，干脆就不愿意干。

root: 英语本土构词：前缀 un-（不）+ willing（愿意的），willing 由 will（意愿；意志）加 -ing 构成，will 可追溯至古英语 willa / willan（愿望、想要）

sensesIntro.en: One missing will shows up as refusal, as grudging compliance, as a forced role, and as slow doubt.
sensesIntro.cn: 一份缺席的意愿，表现为拒绝、勉强照办、被迫担当与迟疑拖沓。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: feet moving forward while the body pulls back.
core.cn: 核心意象：脚往前挪，身子往后拽。

branches.en: The plain branch: the wish to do it is simply absent.
branches.cn: 朴素分支：想做的念头根本没有。

branches.en: The grudging branch: the act is done, the mood is not.
branches.cn: 勉强分支：事做了，情绪不在。

branches.en: The role branch: people placed where they never chose.
branches.cn: 角色分支：被放进从未选择的位置。

branches.en: The denial branch: a truth that will not be admitted.
branches.cn: 否认分支：不愿承认的事实。

branches.en: The hesitation branch: an answer that arrives late.
branches.cn: 迟疑分支：迟迟才到的回答。

intro.en: A native negative prefix and a very old suffix sit on the noun for the will.
intro.cn: 本土否定前缀与一个古老的词尾都压在表示「意愿」的名词上。

latinIntro.en: The word is Germanic; the Latin verb for wishing is velle, whose noun is voluntas.
latinIntro.cn: 这个词属日耳曼语；拉丁语中表示意愿的动词是 velle，名词为 voluntas。

items.example: She lost the will to argue.

items.meaningCN: 表示状态或性质的名词后缀

definition_zh: 不情愿地；勉强地；不得已地
definition_en: in a way that shows one does not want to do something
core_image: 脚步磨着地面，一点一点往前移
scene: 图书馆要关门了，管理员第三次催人，男生才慢慢合上书。He unwillingly left the reading room when the lights went out.
sceneCN: 这里 unwillingly 是「不情愿地」（第 1 个义项：不愿意却还是做了）；句意为灯灭时他才不得不离开阅览室。脚步磨着地面一点点往前移，正是这个词的核心。

derivatives.zh: 去掉副词词尾 -ly 后得到的形容词，义为「不愿意的」
形容词加 -ness 构成名词，义为「不愿；勉强」
去掉否定前缀后的肯定形式，义为「乐意地」
同源名词，义为「意愿；意志」

senses.title: Doing something without wanting to
senses.definition: doing what is asked while making clear that one does not want to
senses.definitionCN: 照要求去做，同时表明自己并不愿意
senses.example: She unwillingly agreed to sing at the party.
senses.exampleCN: 她勉强答应在聚会上唱歌。
senses.why: The adverb simply carries the idea of an absent will onto the verb: the action runs against the wish.
senses.whyCN: 这个副词把「意愿缺席」直接带到动词上：动作与心愿背道而驰。

senses.title: Parting with something with regret
senses.definition: giving something up while still wanting to keep it
senses.definitionCN: 把东西交出去，心里却还想留着
senses.example: He unwillingly handed the keys to the new owner.
senses.exampleCN: 他不情愿地把钥匙交给新主人。
senses.why: The adverb turns the absent will toward an object, and what one still wants to keep leaves the hand slowly.
senses.whyCN: 副词把缺席的意愿指向某个对象，于是还想留着的东西就这么慢慢离开了手。

senses.title: Accepting a fact one would rather deny
senses.definition: admitting something only because the evidence leaves no choice
senses.definitionCN: 只因证据不容否认才承认某事
senses.example: She unwillingly admitted that the plan had failed.
senses.exampleCN: 她勉强承认这个计划失败了。
senses.why: Resistance to the act becomes resistance to the truth, and admission is the act forced by evidence.
senses.whyCN: 对动作的抵触变成对事实的抵触，而承认正是被证据逼出来的动作。

senses.title: Obeying an order without agreement
senses.definition: following an order while disagreeing with it
senses.definitionCN: 在不认同的情况下照命令行事
senses.example: The clerk unwillingly followed the new rule.
senses.exampleCN: 店员不得已照新规定办事。
senses.why: A will that is absent does not stop the feet; obedience without agreement is what remains.
senses.whyCN: 意愿缺席并不能让脚停下来，剩下就是「照做却不同意」。

senses.title: Getting out of bed or leaving a place
senses.definition: moving slowly because one has no wish to go
senses.definitionCN: 因为不想去而动作迟缓
senses.example: They unwillingly got up when the alarm rang again.
senses.exampleCN: 闹钟又响时，他们才磨磨蹭蹭地起床。
senses.why: When no wish moves the body, the body moves slowly, so the adverb also names dragging feet.
senses.whyCN: 没有意愿推动身体，身体就走得慢，于是这个副词也用来形容拖沓的脚步。

intro.en: A negative prefix, the old noun for will, a participle ending, and the adverb ending stack in a clear line.
intro.cn: 否定前缀、古老的「意愿」名词、分词词尾与副词词尾依次清晰地叠加。

items.en: Willa meant wish, and un- was already used to deny a quality.
items.cn: willa 意为「愿望」，un- 当时已用于否定某种性质。

items.en: Willing is formed from will, and the adverb adds -ly to make willingly.
items.cn: willing 由 will 构成，副词再加 -ly 得到 willingly。

items.en: Unwilling follows the same pattern with the negative prefix in front.
items.cn: unwilling 以同样的方式构成，只是前面加了否定前缀。

items.en: Unwillingly appears as the regular adverb in written usage from the modern period.
items.cn: unwillingly 作为规则副词在现代时期的书面语中出现。

items.en: It is common with verbs of agreeing, accepting, and parting.
items.cn: 它常与「同意、接受、割舍」一类的动词连用。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers adverbs built on will, and the near-meaning group collects adverbs of reluctance.
note.cn: 形近组汇集建在 will 上的副词，近义组汇集表示不情愿的副词。

normalIntro.en: Four familiar pieces stack in a row: not, will, the participle ending, and the adverb ending.
normalIntro.cn: 四个熟悉的部分依次叠起：否定、意愿、分词词尾与副词词尾。

normal.en: Break it as un- plus willing plus -ly, and nothing is left unexplained.
normal.cn: 拆成 un- 加 willing 加 -ly，就没有解释不了的部分。

normal.en: It usually sits after the verb or at the front of the clause.
normal.cn: 它通常放在动词后或从句前部。

normal.en: Agree unwillingly and leave unwillingly are the two solid collocations.
normal.cn: agree unwillingly 与 leave unwillingly 是两个扎实的搭配。

normal.en: Reluctantly is close but stresses hesitation, not will.
normal.cn: reluctantly 意思相近，但强调的是迟疑而非意愿。

normal.en: The adjective form is the adjective to learn first.
normal.cn: 先记住形容词形式，副词只是加 -ly。

abstract.en: Hear shoes scraping slowly on a wooden floor.
abstract.cn: 听鞋子在木地板上磨蹭的声音。

abstract.en: See keys dropped into another palm one by one.
abstract.cn: 看见钥匙一把一把落进别人的掌心。

abstract.en: Watch a hand push a door open and hold it back.
abstract.cn: 看一只手把门推开，又往回带。

examples.en: He unwillingly signed the form and pushed it back across the desk.
examples.cn: 他不情愿地签了表，又从桌上推了回去。

examples.en: The children unwillingly turned off the game when dinner was called.
examples.cn: 听到喊吃饭，孩子们不情愿地关掉了游戏。

examples.en: She unwillingly admitted that the plan had failed.
examples.cn: 她勉强承认这个计划失败了。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「俺不灵了」——心里一直念着俺不灵了，手上的活儿就做得磨磨蹭蹭。

root: 英语本土构词：un-（不）+ will（意愿）+ -ing（分词词尾）+ -ly（副词词尾），will 源自古代英语 willa / willan

sensesIntro.en: One adverb for acting against the wish covers consent, parting, admission, obedience, and slow departure.
sensesIntro.cn: 一个表示「违背心愿而做」的副词，覆盖答应、割舍、承认、服从与磨蹭离开。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: shoes scraping along the floor.
core.cn: 核心意象：鞋底在地上磨着走。

branches.en: The consent branch: a yes that sounds like a sigh.
branches.cn: 答应分支：一声答应带着叹息。

branches.en: The parting branch: something leaves the hand slowly.
branches.cn: 割舍分支：东西慢慢离开手心。

branches.en: The admission branch: a truth spoken under pressure.
branches.cn: 承认分支：被逼出来的实话。

branches.en: The obedience branch: an order followed with no agreement.
branches.cn: 服众分支：照着命令做却不认同。

branches.en: The departure branch: leaving one step at a time.
branches.cn: 离开分支：一步一停地走。

intro.en: Four common pieces in a row, each still clear in the meaning.
intro.cn: 四个常见部件依次排列，各自的含义仍然清楚。

latinIntro.en: The base is Germanic; in Latin the matching adverb would be built on invitus, unwilling.
latinIntro.cn: 词根属日耳曼语；拉丁语中对应的副词要建在 invitus（不情愿的）上。

items.example: He had no will to fight.

definition_zh: 向上；起来；在上面；（数量）上升；（时间）到；完成；沿……而上
definition_en: towards a higher place, position, or level, or into an active or finished state
core_image: 一只手从低处把东西往上托
scene: 工地上吊绳绷紧，一捆钢筋从坑底慢慢露出地面。The load came up out of the pit slowly.
sceneCN: 这里 up 是「向上」（第 1 个义项：由低处升高处）；句意为那捆货从坑底慢慢升上来。一只手从低处把东西往上托，正是这个词的核心。

pos.zh: 向上的；已完成的；醒着的

derivatives.zh: 由 up 加比较级词尾构成，义为「上部的；较高的」
由 up 加 -ward 构成，义为「向上的；朝上」
由 up 与 stairs 复合，义为「在楼上；上楼」
由 up 与 set 复合，原义「打翻」，引申为「使心烦」

senses.title: Towards a higher place
senses.definition: towards a higher place or position
senses.definitionCN: 朝更高的地方或位置
senses.example: She looked up at the clock and frowned.
senses.exampleCN: 她抬头看了看钟，皱起眉头。
senses.why: The word began as a Germanic adverb of upward motion, and that physical direction is still its centre.
senses.whyCN: 这个词起初是日耳曼语中表示向上运动的副词，这一物理方向至今仍是它的中心。

senses.title: Into a standing or active state
senses.definition: into a standing, awake, or working state
senses.definitionCN: 进入站起、醒着或运转的状态
senses.example: He got up as soon as the bell rang.
senses.exampleCN: 铃声一响他就站了起来。
senses.why: Rising from the ground is also rising into activity, so standing up and waking up share one word.
senses.whyCN: 从地面升起也就是进入活动状态，因此「站起来」与「醒来」共用一个词。

senses.title: Along a road or a slope
senses.definition: used as a preposition for movement along or higher on something
senses.definitionCN: 作介词，表示沿某物前行或在其较高处
senses.example: They walked up the hill without speaking.
senses.exampleCN: 他们一言不发地走上山坡。
senses.why: Walking up a slope is the same upward motion, so the adverb easily becomes a preposition of route.
senses.whyCN: 沿坡行走还是同一个向上的动作，因此这个副词很容易转为表示路径的介词。

senses.title: Increasing in number or level
senses.definition: used of prices, numbers, or levels that rise
senses.definitionCN: 用于价格、数字或水平的升高
senses.example: Sales went up sharply in the last quarter.
senses.exampleCN: 上季度销量急剧上升。
senses.why: Numbers move in space in everyday speech, so a rising figure is simply a thing that goes up.
senses.whyCN: 日常说法里数字也在空间中移动，于是数值上升就是一样东西「往上去了」。

senses.title: Finished or out of time
senses.definition: used when a period or supply has come to its end
senses.definitionCN: 表示一段时间或供给已经到尽头
senses.example: Time is up, so put your pens down.
senses.exampleCN: 时间到了，把笔放下吧。
senses.why: A measure filled to the top can rise no further, and that image gives the sense of finished.
senses.whyCN: 容器装到顶就再升不上去了，这个意象生出「结束、用完」的意思。

senses.title: As far as a stated number
senses.definition: used with to for the greatest number reached
senses.definitionCN: 与 to 连用，表示所达到的最大数目
senses.example: The hall holds up to three hundred people.
senses.exampleCN: 这个大厅最多能容纳三百人。
senses.why: If up means reaching a point higher on a scale, then up to names the point where a number stops.
senses.whyCN: 既然 up 指沿某一刻度到达更高处，那么 up to 就指出数字停下的那一点。

intro.en: One of the oldest words in English, an adverb of place before it was anything else.
intro.cn: 英语中最古老的词之一，它首先是表示方位的副词。

items.en: The reconstructed form upp means up, and it has relatives in Dutch and German.
items.cn: 重构形式 upp 意为「向上」，在荷兰语和德语中都有同源词。

items.en: The adverb up is recorded early, with the comparative upper forming alongside it.
items.cn: 副词 up 很早就有记录，比较级 upper 也随之形成。

items.en: It is used with verbs of motion, as in standan up, to stand up.
items.cn: 它常与运动动词连用，如 standan up（站起来）。

items.en: Everyday phrases such as get up and up to now fix the word as a particle.
items.cn: get up、up to now 这类日常短语把它固定为小品词。

items.en: The sense of finished or used up appears in time is up and the gas is up.
items.cn: 「结束、用完」的含义出现在 time is up 与 the gas is up 这类说法里。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers compounds and derivatives of up, while the near-meaning group compares direction and degree words.
note.cn: 形近组汇集 up 的复合词与派生词，近义组比较方向与程度词。

entries.definition: on or to a higher floor

normalIntro.en: A tiny word with a very long history, best learned through its verb phrases.
normalIntro.cn: 一个历史极悠久的小词，最好的记法是通过它与动词组成的短语。

normal.en: Learn up through verbs: get up, look up, stand up, give up.
normal.cn: 通过动词记：get up、look up、stand up、give up。

normal.en: Up plus to means as far as, either in number or in time.
normal.cn: up 加 to 意为「达到」，可用于数目或时间。

normal.en: Upper is the older comparative of up, not a separate root.
normal.cn: upper 是 up 较古老的比较级，并非另一个词根。

normal.en: Up and down together make the picture of repeated movement.
normal.cn: up and down 连用画出反复移动的画面。

normal.en: Time is up uses up as finished, not as direction.
normal.cn: time is up 里的 up 表示「结束」，不是方向。

abstract.en: Watch a hand lift something out of a pit.
abstract.cn: 想象一只手把东西从坑里托出来。

abstract.en: Feel a rope tighten and a bucket rise.
abstract.cn: 体会绳子绷紧、桶子升起。

abstract.en: See a hand switch a lamp on.
abstract.cn: 看一只手把灯打开。

examples.en: The children ran up the hill to see the sea.
examples.cn: 孩子们跑上山去看海。

examples.en: Prices went up again in the spring.
examples.cn: 价格在春天又一次上涨。

examples.en: Time is up, and the exam papers must be handed in.
examples.cn: 时间到了，试卷必须交上来。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「阿普」——搬东西时喊着阿普阿普，众人一起用力把重物往上抬。

root: 古英语 up（副词），源自日耳曼语重构形式 upp，与荷兰语 op、德语 auf 同源，本义「向上」

sensesIntro.en: One upward motion supplies direction, then standing, then rising levels, finally finishing and reaching a limit.
sensesIntro.cn: 一个向上的动作先给方向，再给站立，再给上升，最后给结束与达到极限。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a hand lifting something from below.
core.cn: 核心意象：一只手从下面把东西抬起。

branches.en: The direction branch: eyes and objects go higher.
branches.cn: 方向分支：视线与物件往高处去。

branches.en: The state branch: up means awake, standing, working.
branches.cn: 状态分支：up 指醒着、站着、运转着。

branches.en: The preposition branch: along or higher on a road.
branches.cn: 介词分支：沿路而行或位于高处。

branches.en: The figure branch: numbers that keep climbing.
branches.cn: 数字分支：一路往上爬的数值。

branches.en: The limit branch: used up, and as far as a number.
branches.cn: 极限分支：用完了，以及达到某个数目。

intro.en: A bare Germanic adverb that now works as particle, preposition, adjective, and noun.
intro.cn: 一个光秃秃的日耳曼语副词，如今可作小品词、介词、形容词与名词。

latinIntro.en: Latin expresses the same direction with sursum, upward, and the prefix super-.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语用 sursum（向上）与前缀 super- 表达同一方向。

items.meaning: to raise to a better level

definition_zh: 在……之上；一……就；在……之后立即；依据；关于
definition_en: on, or immediately after something happens, or used to introduce the basis of something
core_image: 手按下去，正好落在桌面上
scene: 老人把手掌贴在旧相册的封面上，久久没有说话。He laid his hand upon the cover and was silent for a while.
sceneCN: 这里 upon 是「在……之上」（第 1 个义项：接触并覆在某物上）；句意为他把手放在封面上，沉默了好一会儿。手掌落上桌面的画面，正是这个词的核心。

derivatives.zh: 同义而更常用的形式，义为「在……上」
由 there 与 upon 复合，义为「随即；因此」
由 where 与 upon 复合，义为「于是；随即」

senses.title: Resting on a surface
senses.definition: in contact with the top of something
senses.definitionCN: 与某个物体的上表面接触
senses.example: He set the cup upon the table.
senses.exampleCN: 他把杯子放在桌面上。
senses.why: The word is a strengthened form of on, and the physical contact with a surface is its first sense.
senses.whyCN: 这个词是 on 的加强形式，与表面的实物接触是它的第一层意思。

senses.title: Immediately after something happens
senses.definition: at the moment of, or right after, an event
senses.definitionCN: 在某个事件发生之时或紧接其后
senses.example: Upon hearing the news, she dropped the phone.
senses.exampleCN: 一听到消息，她就把电话掉了。
senses.why: Whatever lies upon something arrives touching it at once, and this contact becomes immediate succession.
senses.whyCN: 放在某物之上的东西会立刻贴上它，这种接触便化为「紧接而来」。

senses.title: Used for the basis of a decision
senses.definition: used to introduce what a decision or belief rests on
senses.definitionCN: 用于引出决定或信念所依托之物
senses.example: The judge acted upon the evidence in the file.
senses.exampleCN: 法官依据卷宗里的证据行事。
senses.why: A decision resting on evidence is like a weight resting on a table, so the word marks the ground beneath it.
senses.whyCN: 决定依托证据，就像重物托在桌面上，于是这个词用来标出底下的那块地面。

senses.title: Used in formal statements of obligation
senses.definition: used to name who carries a duty or a blame
senses.definitionCN: 用于指明义务或过失由谁承担
senses.example: The duty fell upon the youngest son.
senses.exampleCN: 这份责任落在了最小的儿子身上。
senses.why: A duty set on a person is literally a load placed on a surface, and the image transfers to responsibility.
senses.whyCN: 落在某人身上的义务，字面上就是压在某个表面上的一份重量，于是这个画面转成了责任。

senses.title: Frozen in story openings
senses.definition: kept in the fixed phrase that begins folk tales
senses.definitionCN: 保留在童话开头固定说法里
senses.example: Once upon a time a shop stood on this corner.
senses.exampleCN: 从前这个街角开着一家店。
senses.why: The tale's first scene is placed upon a time, and the phrase has not changed for centuries.
senses.whyCN: 故事的第一个场景被「搁在」一段时间上，这个说法几百年都没变。

intro.en: Two old prepositions, one piled on the other for emphasis.
intro.cn: 两个古老的介词，一个叠在另一个之上以加强语气。

items.en: On is ancient, and up is an old adverb of motion upward.
items.cn: on 十分古老，up 则是表示向上运动的古副词。

items.en: The compound uppon puts the two together with the sense of resting on top of.
items.cn: 复合形式 uppon 把两者合起来，意为「覆于其上」。

items.en: Upon competes with on and keeps a more formal and literary tone.
items.cn: upon 与 on 并用，但保留了更正式、更书卷的语气。

items.en: Upon fixes itself in set phrases such as once upon a time and upon request.
items.cn: upon 固定在 once upon a time、upon request 等熟语里。

items.en: The sense of immediately after develops in formal writing.
items.cn: 「紧接其后」的含义在正式书面语中发展出来。

note.en: The look-alike group shows other up- words that are not related, while the near-meaning group compares prepositions of position and time.
note.cn: 形近组列出与 up 相关但无词源关联的其他词，近义组比较位置与时间介词。

entries.definitionCN: 上部的（只是拼写相近，词源不同）

entries.definition: to support, as a court does
entries.definitionCN: 维护；支持（只是拼写相近，词源不同）
打翻；使心烦（只是拼写相近，词源不同）

normalIntro.en: A piled-up preposition, formal in tone, alive mostly in fixed phrases.
normalIntro.cn: 一个叠加而成的介词，语气正式，主要活在固定短语里。

normal.en: Think of upon as on with an extra push of up.
normal.cn: 把 upon 想成 on 加上 up 的一推。

normal.en: Once upon a time is the phrase every learner already knows.
normal.cn: once upon a time 是学习者早已会说的短语。

normal.en: Upon request and upon arrival show the formal register.
normal.cn: upon request 与 upon arrival 显示出正式语气。

normal.en: Rely upon and depend upon are equally correct with on.
normal.cn: rely upon、depend upon 与用 on 一样正确。

normal.en: Upon hearing is the common frame for immediately after.
normal.cn: upon hearing 是表示「一听到就」的常见框架。

abstract.en: Press a palm flat on a book cover.
abstract.cn: 把掌心平平按在书封上。

abstract.en: See one stone laid exactly on another.
abstract.cn: 看一块石头正好压在另一块上。

abstract.en: Hear a door open the instant a knock ends.
abstract.cn: 听敲门声一停，门就开了。

examples.en: She placed the letter upon the desk and turned away.
examples.cn: 她把信放在桌上，转身走了。

examples.en: Upon arriving at the station, he called his mother.
examples.cn: 一到车站，他就给母亲打了电话。

examples.en: The committee decided upon the plan after a long debate.
examples.cn: 经过长时间辩论，委员会就这个方案作出了决定。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「额碰」——低头太急，额碰在桌沿上，正好碰在桌面这个「之上」的位置。

root: 古英语复合形式 uppon，由 up（向上）与 on（在……上）合并而成，本义「覆于其上」，与 on 同源同义而语气更正式

sensesIntro.en: Contact with a surface gives rest, then immediate succession, then grounds, then duty, then a story opening.
sensesIntro.cn: 与表面的接触先给「搁置」，再给「紧接」，再给依据、义务，最后给故事开头。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a palm pressed flat on a surface.
core.cn: 核心意象：一只手掌平压在表面上。

branches.en: The surface branch: a thing set down and in contact.
branches.cn: 表面分支：放下去并贴着的东西。

branches.en: The time branch: contact becomes immediate succession.
branches.cn: 时间分支：接触变成紧接其后。

branches.en: The ground branch: what a decision stands on.
branches.cn: 根据分支：决定所踩的地面。

branches.en: The duty branch: blame resting on someone.
branches.cn: 义务分支：落在某人身上的责任。

branches.en: The story branch: the fixed opening of a tale.
branches.cn: 故事分支：故事固定的开头。

intro.en: A compound preposition whose two parts are both very old and still in daily use.
intro.cn: 一个复合介词，两个部分都非常古老，且今天仍在使用。

latinIntro.en: Latin uses super for on top of and in plus a noun for the time sense.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语用 super 表示「在……之上」，时间义则用 in 加名词。

items.example: The book is on the desk.
Upon arrival, report to the desk.
Once upon a time a girl lived here.
items.exampleCN: 从前有个姑娘住在这里。

items.example: We rely upon the river for water.

definition_zh: 上面的；较高的；上部的；上游的；上层的；（地位）较高的
definition_en: higher in position or rank than something else
core_image: 两层抽屉，上面那层要抬手才够得着
scene: 书架从地面一直顶到天花板，最上面那几排书要搬梯子才拿得到。The upper shelves are full of old magazines.
sceneCN: 这里 upper 是「上面的」（第 1 个义项：位置较高的）；句意为上面几层书架塞满了旧杂志。抬手才够得着的上层抽屉，正是这个词的核心。

derivatives.zh: 由 upper 加 -most 构成，义为「最高的；最上面的」
upper 的比较级词尾所由来的原副词，义为「向上」
由 up 加 -wards 构成，义为「向上；朝上」

senses.title: Higher of two parts
senses.definition: higher in position when two parts are compared
senses.definitionCN: 比较两部分时位置较高的那一部分
senses.example: The upper drawer holds the knives.
senses.exampleCN: 上面那层抽屉放的是刀。
senses.why: The word is the old comparative of up, so it simply means the more up of two things.
senses.whyCN: 这个词是 up 较古老的比较级，字面就是「两者中更靠上的那个」。

senses.title: Near the top of a building or body
senses.definition: used of the part of a building or a body nearer the top
senses.definitionCN: 形容建筑或身体靠近顶端的部分
senses.example: He lives on the upper floor of the old house.
senses.exampleCN: 他住在这栋老房子的楼上。
senses.why: A building is vertical, so the part nearer the roof is literally the more up part.
senses.whyCN: 建筑是竖着的，因此靠近屋顶的那部分字面上就是「更靠上的一端」。

senses.title: Higher in rank or class
senses.definition: used of people of higher social or official rank
senses.definitionCN: 形容社会或职务等级较高的人
senses.example: The upper class lived behind the park.
senses.exampleCN: 上层人家住在公园后面。
senses.why: Social rank is pictured as height, and the higher people are said to be in, the more the word applies.
senses.whyCN: 社会等级被画成了高度，人所在的位置越「高」，这个词就用得越贴切。

senses.title: Further up a river
senses.definition: used of the part of a river further from the sea
senses.definitionCN: 形容河流离海较远的一段
senses.example: They swam in the upper reaches of the river.
senses.exampleCN: 他们在河的上游河段游泳。
senses.why: A river runs downhill, so the higher part of the land gives the upper part of the stream.
senses.whyCN: 河往低处流，因此地势较高的那一段就成了溪流的上游。

senses.title: The higher of two limits
senses.definition: used of the highest figure allowed or recorded
senses.definitionCN: 形容允许或记录的最高数值
senses.example: The upper limit for the room is twenty people.
senses.exampleCN: 这个房间的上限是二十人。
senses.why: Two bounds are compared exactly as two shelves are, and the higher one takes the word.
senses.whyCN: 两条界限的比较与两层架子的比较完全一样，较高的那条就用这个词。

senses.title: The top of a shoe
senses.definition: the part of a shoe above the sole
senses.definitionCN: 鞋底以上的部分
senses.example: The uppers are leather, the soles are rubber.
senses.exampleCN: 鞋帮是皮的，鞋底是橡胶的。
senses.why: The part of a shoe that rises above the sole is named by the same word that means the higher of two.
senses.whyCN: 鞋底之上升高起来的那部分，用的仍是表示「较高者」的这个词。

intro.en: The old comparative of up, kept as a separate adjective while the verb moved on.
intro.cn: up 的古老比较级形式，在其他用法继续演变时被保留为独立形容词。

items.en: The root upp means up, and a comparative form existed early in the family.
items.cn: 词根 upp 意为「向上」，这一语族很早就有了比较级形式。

items.en: The word yferra served as the comparative of up and meant higher.
items.cn: 古英语 yferra 充当 up 的比较级，意为「更高的」。

items.en: The form develops into upper, while up remains an adverb and particle.
items.cn: 这一形式后来发展为 upper，而 up 保持副词与小品词的身份。

items.en: Upper takes on social meaning in upper class and upper house.
items.cn: upper 在 upper class、upper house 中获得社会与制度义。

items.en: Concrete uses such as shoe uppers and upper limit keep the word physical.
items.cn: upper 也用于鞋帮、上限这类具体说法，保持着实感。

note.en: The look-alike group collects up- words and their compounds, while the near-meaning group compares words for height and rank.
note.cn: 形近组收集 up 系词及其复合词，近义组比较表示高低与等级的词。

normalIntro.en: One of the few words in English that preserves an old comparative ending outside the usual two-tier pattern.
normalIntro.cn: 英语中少数保留了古老比较级词尾、却不属于通常两级体系的词之一。

normal.en: Upper is the comparison of up, not of a simple adjective.
normal.cn: upper 是 up 的比较形式，并非普通形容词的比较级。

normal.en: The upper hand comes from an old game and now means an advantage.
normal.cn: the upper hand 源自一种古老游戏，现在指占上风。

normal.en: Upper class and upper house are the social and political uses.
normal.cn: upper class 与 upper house 是它的社会与政治用法。

normal.en: Uppermost adds -most for the very top.
normal.cn: uppermost 加 -most 表示最顶端。

normal.en: Shoe uppers are the part above the sole.
normal.cn: shoe uppers 指鞋底以上的那部分。

abstract.en: Reach up for the drawer above your head.
abstract.cn: 伸手去够头顶上方的抽屉。

abstract.en: See two shelves and only the high one is full.
abstract.cn: 看见两层架子，只有上面那层是满的。
